means: A 3D-renderer term for light scattering off particles suspended in the air, so the beam has volume. It is the name of a technique, not the name of anything visible.
does: Very little on its own. This is engine-marketing vocabulary from Unreal and Blender, not danbooru vocabulary, so the model has no trained picture filed under it. It is exactly the QUALITY-naming tag this project keeps measuring to be inert - the same class as night and dark background, which together moved mean luma from 170 to 161, i.e. nothing. If you want the shafts, write what is actually in the air: sunbeam, light shafts, dust motes in the beams, hazy air. Those name things the model has seen drawn.
reach_for_it: essentially never on this checkpoint - use god rays / sunbeam / dust motes instead. Keep the word for Qwen prompts, where render and photographic vocabulary does land
used_in: only as filler inside the strong option of studio/cards/light_god_rays.json ('god rays, bold volumetric light beams, sunbeam'), where the two neighbouring tags carry the panel
example_base: 1boy, solo, male focus, short black hair, dark jacket, standing on a rooftop, city skyline behind, late afternoon sun, looking away, masterpiece, best quality, very aesthetic, absurdres
read_it_as: Compare the SHADING, colour and line - not the pose or framing. Adding any clause re-rolls the model's conditioning, so composition moves between the two panels even at a fixed seed. An img2img pass from one fixed base image would isolate the tag properly; that is not built yet.
